run_mode: native venv, served (openai endpoint + `vllm bench serve`, random dataset)
gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97887 MiB, single GPU (sm_120 / cc 12.0, 188 SMs)
model_desc: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, model_type gemma4; MoE 128 experts top-8, ~4B active; 30 layers, hidden 2816, head_dim 256 / global_head_dim 512, 16 Q / 8 KV heads, sliding_window 1024, final_logit_softcapping 30.0)
attention_backend: TRITON_ATTN (forced: Gemma4 has heterogeneous head dims head_dim=256/global_head_dim=512, FA4 unavailable) — same in all three configs

moe_backend.bf16: FlashInfer CUTLASS Unquantized MoE (verbatim: 'Using FlashInfer CUTLASS Unquantized MoE backend out of potential backends: [FlashInfer TRTLLM, FlashInfer CUTLASS, TRITON, BATCHED_TRITON]'); trtllm::fused_moe gemm1/gemm2 autotuned at warmup (21 profiles each, 2 unsupported tactics skipped) — first-server startup took 550 s largely due to this autotune
moe_backend.fp8_and_fp8kv: TRITON Fp8 MoE (verbatim: 'Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend out of potential backends: [AITER, FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, FLASHINFER_CUTLASS, DEEPGEMM, TRITON, MARLIN, HUMMING, BATCHED_DEEPGEMM, BATCHED_TRITON, XPU, CPU, HPC]') with the DEFAULT (untuned) kernel config — vLLM warns 'Using default MoE config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at .../fused_moe/configs/E=128,N=704,device_name=NVIDIA_RTX_PRO_6000_Blackwell_Server_Edition,dtype=fp8_w8a8.json'. Dense linears use CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel (Fp8PerTensorOnlineLinearMethod).

cuda_graphs: ON (not --enforce-eager); cudagraph_mode FULL_AND_PIECEWISE; 'Graph capturing finished in 11-16 secs, took 0.45-0.47 GiB' in every config
sanity: per-config chat gate ('What is the capital of France?' -> 'The capital of France is **Paris**.'); coherent in all three configs — including the fp8-quantized MoE
schema: each config.results row = {input_len, ttft_ms, prefill_tok_s, tpot_ms, itl_ms, decode_tok_s}
prefill_tok_s_convention: DERIVED as input_len / (Mean_TTFT_ms/1000) by the harness. vLLM bench serve reports no standalone prefill throughput; TTFT includes prefill + the first decode token + scheduling, so this slightly UNDER-reports true prefill tok/s. Kept for consistency with the repo's other served vLLM files (same derivation).
notes: Same harness as the 12B/31B runs (gemma4-12b-vllm-sm120.json, gemma4-31b-vllm-sm120.json): scratch copy of perf-data/bench_vllm_cuda.sh with ONE line changed — the hardcoded CUDA-12.8 PATH (line 58) replaced by PATH=/workspace/venvs/vllm/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:$PATH. Same CTXS/MAXLEN/GPU_UTIL for all three configs.

vLLM 0.25.1 routes this MoE correctly on sm_120 in ALL THREE configs: sanity chat is coherent, including fp8 quantization of the 128-expert MoE. fp8 MoE support status: WORKS, but runs the Triton fp8 MoE kernel on a DEFAULT (untuned) config for this GPU (no E=128,N=704 fp8_w8a8 tuning file ships for RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) — vLLM itself warns performance may be sub-optimal. That headroom is baseline data.

MoE means fp8's decode win is smaller than on the dense models: only the ~4B active parameters stream per token, so weight-quantization saves less bandwidth (-15% to -24% TPOT vs bf16, versus ~-40% on the dense 31B).

fp8 does NOT improve TTFT over bf16 on this model (87.85 vs 75.34 ms at 1k; within noise 16k-128k): prefill is compute-bound in the untuned Triton fp8 MoE path, while bf16 prefill rides the autotuned FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE. fp8kv is the only config that cuts long-ctx TTFT (128k: 5.13 s vs 9.29/9.62 s).
NO OOM and NO failed points: all 3 configs x 7 contexts (1k..128k) completed. gpu-memory-utilization CONSTANT at 0.90.
DECODE metric = tpot_ms (== itl_ms at concurrency 1). Lower is better; this is the campaign target.

ctx=1024 ttft_ms carries first-shape warm-up (torch.compile specialization / cudagraph capture for the smallest bench shape); a chat warm-up request precedes the sweep but the 1024 point still sees some of it. Decode TPOT is unaffected.
bf16 server first became healthy after 550 s (flashinfer trtllm::fused_moe gemm1/gemm2 autotune at warmup); fp8/fp8kv in 200-205 s.
fp8kv config logs 'Checkpoint does not provide a q scaling factor. Setting it to k_scale' — harmless here (only matters for FP8 flash-attn/flashinfer attention backends; this run is TRITON_ATTN).

Every GPU-touching command ran inside `gpulease b1-26b ...`; one lease per config spanning serve -> sweep -> shutdown -> VRAM drain. The fp8kv lease ran later than bf16/fp8 (the original driver process was killed while queued behind other agents' leases; the config was re-launched identically).

configs.moe_backend: FlashInfer CUTLASS Unquantized MoE (autotuned trtllm::fused_moe at warmup)
notes: ~4B active params make this the fastest decoder of the three B1 models despite the 48.07 GiB checkpoint: bf16 TPOT 7.61-12.34 ms vs the dense 31B's 44.67-55.46 ms.

configs.config_desc: fp8 weight-only (--quantization fp8, dynamic e4m3 from the bf16 ckpt; MoE experts fp8_w8a8 via Triton, dense linears CutlassFP8ScaledMM)
configs.moe_backend: TRITON Fp8 MoE, DEFAULT (untuned) config for E=128,N=704 on this GPU
notes: fp8 quantization of the 128-expert MoE WORKS (coherent sanity output) — decode -15% to -24% TPOT vs bf16, the smaller win expected for a sparse model.
TTFT is NOT better than bf16 (equal to slightly worse across the ladder): the Triton fp8 MoE prefill runs on an untuned default config while bf16 prefill uses autotuned FlashInfer CUTLASS.
fp8 frees ~22 GiB of KV pool vs bf16 (32.42 -> 54.59 GiB).

configs.config_desc: fp8 weights + fp8 KV cache (--quantization fp8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8)
configs.moe_backend: TRITON Fp8 MoE, DEFAULT (untuned) config for E=128,N=704 on this GPU
notes: Same 54.59 GiB KV pool holds 3,369,625 tokens (exactly 2x fp8's 1,684,812) — 25.51x concurrency headroom at 132k, the largest of any B1 config.
fp8kv is the best config at every ctx >= 16k, decode AND prefill: 128k TPOT 8.46 ms (-31% vs bf16, -19% vs fp8), 128k TTFT 5.13 s (-45% vs bf16, -47% vs fp8).
NO 128k decode anomaly here — unlike the dense 31B, fp8kv TPOT scales smoothly through 128k (8 KV heads x 30 layers vs 16 x 60: the fp8-KV TRITON decode kernel stays in its fast regime).
